final.title: When search becomes a workflow decision
final.body:
If you are rethinking search behaviour in a small business, start with one question: are people repeatedly searching your own business material, or the open web? That difference matters. Repeated searching through customer emails, past invoices, product specs, or help-desk notes is a workflow problem; random web research usually is not.

For an owner-operator, the practical threshold is not “should we use AI?” but “is this recurring search taking a noticeable slice of the week and leading to slower replies, more errors, or more back-and-forth?” If yes, treat it as one bounded workflow decision, not a grand AI strategy. Plain old repetition is often the giveaway.

The main control is document readiness. A knowledge assistant only makes sense when the useful material already exists in machine-readable form, such as MD, PDF, or structured data. Bareni has a self-built demo that retrieves from approved company documents rather than the open web. It runs locally on synthetic data; OCR, scan ingestion, rate limiting, and billing are not working in that demo.

Keep human approval in place if the output affects customer communication or business decisions. The system proposes; the owner decides. That is Bareni’s policy for higher-risk steps, not a warranty.

One practical next step is to map one recurring search task on paper, then check whether the source material is ready and whether you still want final review before anything goes out.

defects.reason: This overstates the prerequisite. Approved evidence says the demo can ingest MD, PDF, and URL content, while scan-heavy OCR-dependent workflows are out of scope; it does not support the broader claim that a knowledge assistant only makes sense when material already exists in machine-readable form.
